sections.overview: Triops longicaudatus is a notostracan branchiopod crustacean, known as the summer tadpole shrimp.
sections.identification: Its body is brown to greyish yellow and resembles a tadpole beneath a broad dorsal shield.
sections.habitat: It inhabits warm, temporary freshwater pools, often with muddy or sandy bottoms.
sections.diet: It is omnivorous, feeding on detritus as well as insect larvae and small zooplankton.
sections.behavior: It forages on the pool bottom by day and tends to bury itself in the sediment at night.
sections.reproduction: Its dormant eggs or cysts can remain in dried pool sediment and hatch after water returns.
sections.ecology: It belongs to a mainly American lineage, unlike the largely Palearctic T. cancriformis lineage.
sections.conservation: The Spanish government account warns that released captive animals or cysts could affect native aquatic communities; it is not a global status assessment.
